21

PROJECT SCHEDULE MANAGEMENT 

The main monitoring and controlling process performed as part of project schedule management is controlling the schedule or schedule control. 

Project managers often cite delivering projects on time (schedule control) as one of their biggest challenges, because schedule problems often cause more conflict than other issues. 

During project initiation, priorities and procedures are often most important, but as the project proceeds, especially during the middle and latter stages of a project, schedule issues become the predominant source of 
conflict.

Perhaps part of the reason schedule problems are so common is that time is easily and simply measured. 

After a project schedule is set, anyone can quickly estimate schedule performance by subtracting the original time estimate from the time actually expended.

People often compare planned and actual project completion times without considering the approved project changes. 

Time is also the variable with the least amount of flexibility. 

Time passes no matter what happens on a project. 

Individual work styles and cultural differences may also cause schedule conflicts. For example, one dimension of the MyersBriggs team-building tool that was described in Chapter 6 (Judgment/Perception, or J/P) deals 
with peoples’ attitudes toward structure and deadlines. Some people (J’s) prefer detailed schedules and focus on task completion. Others (P’s) prefer to keep things open and flexible. Different cultures and even entire 
countries have different attitudes about schedules. For example, in some countries, businesses close for several hours every afternoon so workers can take naps. Others observe religious or secular holidays during which 
little work is accomplished. Cultures may also have different perceptions of work ethic—some may value hard work and strict schedules, whereas others may value the ability to remain relaxed and flexible. 

The goal of schedule control is to know the status of the schedule, influence the factors that cause schedule changes,
determine whether the schedule has changed, and manage changes when they occur. Key outputs of schedule control include schedule
forecasts and work performance information. There are several tools and techniques for schedule control, including data analysis (such as
earned value management, as described earlier in this chapter), project management information systems, resource optimization,
and several tools discussed in Chapter 5 (such as critical path method, leads and lags, and schedule compression).

Many project managers believe that tracking Gantt charts are an excellent tool for tracking project schedule performance

PROJECT COST MANAGEMENT 

Cost control includes monitoring cost performance, ensuring that only appropriate project changes are included in a 
revised cost baseline, and informing project stakeholders of authorized changes to the project that will affect costs.

The project management plan, project documents, project funding requirements, work performance data, and 
organizational process assets are inputs to the cost-control process. 

Outputs of cost control include work performance information, cost forecasts, change requests, project 
management plan updates, and project documents updates. Several tools and techniques assist in project cost 
control, including expert judgment, data analysis, project management information systems, and the To-complete 
performance index (TCPI), which is a measure of the cost performance that must be achieved on the remaining 
work in order to meet a specified goal, such as the BAC or EAC. As mentioned in the following What Went Right? 
examples, there is great room for improvement in project cost management in many industries.

PROJECT QUALITY MANAGEMENT 
The main project quality management process for monitoring and controlling is quality control. Key outputs include quality-
control measurements, verified deliverables, work performance information, change requests, project management plan 
updates, and project documents updates. Although one of the main goals of quality control is to ensure and improve quality, 
the main outcomes of this process are acceptance decisions, rework, and process adjustments.
1.
Acceptance decisions determine if the products or services produced as part of the project will be accepted or rejected.
If they are accepted, they are considered to be verified deliverables. If project stakeholders reject some of the products or 
services produced as part of the project, there must be rework.
2.
Rework is action taken to bring rejected items into compliance with product requirements or specifications or other 
stakeholder expectations. Rework can be very expensive, so the project manager who excels at quality planning and quality 
assurance can reduce the need for rework.
3.
Process adjustments correct or prevent further quality problems. Based on the implementation of quality-control
measurements, process adjustments often result in updates to the quality baseline, organizational process assets, and
the project management plan.

Many different tools and techniques are available for performing quality control. The PMBOK® Guide – Sixth Edition, 
lists the following:

Data gathering: Checklists, check sheets, statistical sampling, questionnaires, and surveys




scatter diagrams

Meetings

PROJECT RESOURCE MANAGEMENT 

Controlling resources involves ensuring that the physical resources assigned to the project are available as planned 
and monitoring the planned versus actual resources utilization, taking corrective actions as needed. 

Making effective use of team members is addressed under the Manage Team process. 

Tools and techniques include data analysis, problem solving, interpersonal and team skills, and project 
management information systems. 

Key outputs include work performance information, change requests, project management plan updates, and 
project document updates. 
38

PROJECT COMMUNICATIONS MANAGEMENT 

Monitoring communications involves monitoring communications throughout the project life cycle to ensure that 
stakeholder information needs are met. 

Key outputs include work performance information, change requests, project management plan updates, and 
project documents updates. 

Work performance information focuses on how well project communication is performed compared to what was 
planned. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
39

PROJECT STAKEHOLDER MANAGEMENT 

You cannot control stakeholders, but you can monitor their level of engagement. 

Monitoring stakeholder engagement involves monitoring overall project stakeholder relationships and adjusting 
strategies and plans for engaging stakeholders as needed. 

The project management plan, project documents, work performance data, enterprise environmental factors, and organizational process 
assets are important inputs to this process. 

The project team uses data analysis, decision making, data representation, communication skills, interpersonal and team skills, and 
meetings as the main tools and techniques. 

The outputs of monitoring stakeholder engagement are work performance information, change requests, project management plan 
updates, and project document updates. 

On some projects, stakeholder engagement is monitored by making them key members of the project team. 

It’s important to understand the needs and desires of different types of customers as well. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
40

PROJECT RISK MANAGEMENT 

Monitoring risks involves tracking identified risk events and implementing the risk response plans, while continuing to 
identify and analyze new risks and evaluate risk process effectiveness. 

Project risk management does not stop with the initial risk analysis. 

Identified risk events may not materialize, or their probabilities of occurrence or impact may diminish or increase. 

Similarly, new risk events are normally identified as the project progresses. 

Newly identified risk events need to go through the same process of analysis and monitoring as those identified during the 
initial risk assessment. 

Project teams sometimes use workarounds— unplanned responses to risk events—when they do not have contingency 
plans in place. 

Data analysis (i.e., technical performance measurement and reserve analysis), audits, and meetings are all tools and 
techniques for performing risk monitoring. 

Outputs of this process include work performance information, change requests, project management plan updates, 
project documents updates (especially updating the risk register), and organizational process assets updates. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
41

PROJECT PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT 

Controlling procurements involves managing procurement relationships, monitoring contract performance, making changes and taking 
corrective actions as needed, and closing out contracts. 

Several tools and techniques can help in contract administration, including expert judgment, claims administration, data analysis, inspection, 
and audits. 

In addition to work performance information, change requests, project management plan updates, project documents updates, and 
organizational process asset updates, key outputs of controlling procurements include closed procurements and procurement 
documentation updates. 

It is very important to document all changes to the contract and communicate those changes to all affected stakeholders. 

Project team members must be aware of the potential legal problems of their not understanding a contract. Changes must be handled 
properly for items under contract. 

Professionals in procurement management should be consulted as needed.

It is critical that project managers and team members watch for constructive change orders. Constructive change orders are oral or written 
acts or omissions by someone with actual or apparent authority that can be construed to have the same effect as a written change order. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
42

APPLYING PROJECT MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES TO MONITORING AND
CONTROLLING PROJECTS 

Although several of the project management principles apply to monitoring and controlling projects, the one 
principle that stands out is embracing adaptability and resiliency. 

Adaptability is the ability to respond to changing conditions. 

Resiliency is the ability to absorb impacts and to recover quickly from a setback or failure.

As described throughout this chapter, it’s important for project teams to expect changes, plan for them, and be 
adaptable and resilient in responding to them. Below are a few suggestions to help teams embrace adaptability and 
resiliency:
1.Try to build diverse teams with broad skill sets and experiences
2.Emphasize the importance of continuous learning and improvement
3.Encourage open conversations and new ideas
4.Provide and receive feedback often
5.Focus on meeting desired outcomes instead of just providing planned deliverables 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
44

MONITORING AND CONTROLLING AGILE/HYBRID PROJECTS 

Hybrid projects can use any of the predictive processes, tools, and techniques to monitoring and controlling mentioned so 
far in this chapter as well as any agile approaches they decide will help the project be successful. 

The Scrum Guide (2020) does not mention project control directly, but several events assist in monitoring and controlling 
as follows:

Daily Scrum: “The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as 
necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work.” Developers can also meet throughout the day to discuss adapting or 
replanning the rest of the sprint’s work. 

Sprint Review: “The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations. 
The Scrum Team presents the results of their work to key stakeholders and progress toward the Product Goal is discussed. 
During the event, the Scrum Team and stakeholders review what was accomplished in the Sprint and what has changed in 
their environment. Based on this information, attendees collaborate on what to do next. The Product Backlog may also be 
adjusted to meet new opportunities.”
At the sprint level, Scrum teams often use several artifacts to monitor progress include task boards or Kanban boards, burn 
charts, and velocity charts 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
45

BURN CHARTS

Burn charts show project team velocity. 

“Velocity measures the productivity rate at which the deliverables are produced, validated, and accepted within a predefined interval.”

Burndown charts show the amount of work (number of tasks) remaining compared to the plan. They are often used 
for each sprint and discussed during sprint retrospectives.

Burnup charts show the amount of work (tasks) completed compared to the plan. They can be used during each 
sprint, and they can also show progress for several sprints. Recall that the total amount of planned work often 
changes as the product backlog changes. Burnup charts show changes in planned work.

Combined burn charts show how much work has been completed and how much remains.

MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
46

VELOCITY CHARTS 

Sprint teams use velocity to measure how much work they can complete 
in each iteration. 

It is widely used to help teams create accurate and efficient timelines. 

Sprint team velocity is not constant; rather, it varies. 

Note that velocity charts are not intended to be a tool for monitoring the team. 

They are most useful as a tool for release planning. 

The velocity chart is created after the first sprint and updated after each 
completed sprint. 

The velocity of the sprints helps managers to calibrate the release plan.

“There is no ideal velocity number; an upward trend is not necessarily a good 
thing and a downward trend is not always negative. But both will signal you to 
dig deeper into areas of the development process that can help you achieve 
efficiency while maintaining technical quality.”

business needs. 




CLOSING PROJECT

Closing Project includes archiving project information, ensuring the planned work is complete, and releasing
organizational resources. 

It often includes a final presentation and report. 

For both projects that are completed and those that are canceled before completion, it is important to formally
close the project and reflect on what can be learned to improve future projects. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI

COMMON WAYS TO CLOSE OR TERMINATE A PROJECT
1.
Integration: A project is completed, and products and services created are integrated into operations. 
This is the most common approach. Project staff and other resources are released and distributed into the organization.
2.
Addition: A project creates a new product or service that results in a new unit in the organization, such as a 
department, division, or company. Project staff and other resources move into the new unit.
3.
Extinction: A project may end because it was successful and achieved its goals, and there is no need for further 
work. 
Another form of extinction is when a project is stopped because it was unsuccessful or superseded. A special case of termination by 
extinction, when there is a sudden end to a project.
4.
Starvation: A project can also be terminated by decreasing its budget or suddenly ending funding. 
This approach is also known as withdrawal of life support. The reason for starving a project is generally to shadow the failure of no 
accomplishment of the goals. Management sometimes uses this approach to avoid embarrassment.

2. Final product, service, or result transition: Project sponsors are usually most interested in making sure that 
the final products, services, or results are delivered and transitioned to the appropriate part of the 
organization. 
3. Final report: A final project report and presentation are also commonly used during project closing. 
4. Updates to organizational process assets: Examples of organizational process assets include plans, 
processes, policies, procedures, and knowledge bases, such as templates and lessons-learned reports.

KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER
Knowledge transfer is the process of communicating knowledge that was developed by one person 
or in one part of an organization to another person or other parts of an organization. 
In particular, people who will take over products or results produced as part of the project would 
need to spend time with project team members so they understand what is involved in detail. 
Many organizations are working hard to improve the knowledge transfer process, since employee 
knowledge or human capital is one of their key assets. 
It is crucial, therefore, to make project knowledge transfer a priority, especially if the benefits of a 
project are not achieved immediately. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
15

CLOSING AGILE/HYBRID PROJECTS

Daily Scrum: You can think of these meetings as providing closure for the day before. Teams focus on progress toward
the sprint goal and produce an actionable plan for the next day of work. If there are impediments, they address them
quickly. If the team is not following the Scrum values or processes, corrections are made. Project managers (or Scrum 
masters, or any team member, in fact) must always be aware of people on their team and address any obvious or subtle 
problems.

Sprint reviews: Sprint reviews provide closure for sprints, and sometimes entire projects. Stakeholders provide
feedback at sprint reviews, inspect the outcome of the sprint, and determine future adaptations. If customers do
not see value in what the team produced, they can suggest no future sprints. Remember that sprints can be one month
or less. If requirements change quickly, it might make sense to have sprints that only last a week or even less.

Sprint retrospectives: The team discusses what went well during the sprint, what problems it encountered, and how
those problems were or were not solved. They identify changes to improve team effectiveness and address them
as soon as possible. This event is similar to a lessons learned, but it only focuses on a particular sprint. When a
project ends, teams should hold a final retrospective to focus on all lessons learned. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
16

CLOSING AGILE/HYBRID PROJECTS
Similar to a predictive project close-out meeting, participants should review: 
1. The goals and outcomes of the project
2. Main changes that occurred during the project and how they were addressed
3. The main lessons learned on the project
4. A summary of the transition plan 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
17

ADVICE ON CLOSING PROJECTS
Although project teams (predictive, agile, and hybrid) do not typically spend much time on closing projects, it is important to do 
it well.

It is important to plan for project closing. On a predictive project, there should be deliverables in the WBS and resources 
allocated to perform project closing. 

It will be much easier to close a project if the project team captures lessons learned and other important information 
required for closing as soon as possible. 

For example, the project team should have a lessons-learned repository where everyone can document lessons learned as they occur. A simple blog 
would work well for this purpose, or team members could document lessons learned as part of progress reports. Because many agile teams prefer 
discussing information instead of documenting it, capturing key points in some fashion, like a blog, would also be appropriate. 

Project managers should take time to thank their team and other project stakeholders and have some type of closing
celebration. 

Just having a team lunch or informal gathering might be appropriate, or having a virtual celebration of some sort is appreciated, as long as you 
make it fun! If it was a big, highly successful project, a more formal celebration and rewards would be appropriate. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
18

CHAPTER SUMMARY

Closing projects or phases involves finalizing all activities and bringing the project or phase to an orderly end. 

It includes archiving project information, ensuring the planned work is complete, and releasing organizational resources. 

Closing outputs related to integration management include project documents updates, final products, services, or result 
transition, a final report, and updates to organizational process assets. 

It is also good practice to hold a close-out meeting and hold some type of celebration when a project is over. 

Agile/hybrid projects also include closing activities. 

Teams should transition work to operational groups as needed, hold a project close-out meeting, hold a final retrospective 
to review lessons learned for the entire project, and celebrate the project’s end. 

Helpful advice for closing projects includes planning for closure, documenting lessons learned and other important 
information as soon as possible, and celebrating project closure. 
MANAJEMEN PROYEK TI 2020 – FASILKOM UI
19

Makanan di Kantin Kampus 
Latar Belakang 
Kampus XYZ memiliki banyak kantin yang tersebar di banyak Fakultas. Namun, tidak semua

sebuah aplikasi pemesanan dan pengantaran makanan yang memungkinkan mahasiswa 
memesan makanan dari berbagai tenant di kantin melalui aplikasi.

1.​ Pemesanan makanan secara online dari berbagai tenant kantin. 
2.​ Pengantaran makanan ke lokasi tertentu di dalam area kampus. 
3.​ Pembayaran digital untuk meminimalisir transaksi tunai.

○​ Memesan makanan dengan opsi pengantaran atau pengambilan langsung.

○​ Melacak status pesanan (Dipesan, Diproses, Dikirim, Selesai). 
○​ Memberikan ulasan dan rating.

○​ Mengelola menu dan harga. 
○​ Melihat pesanan yang masuk dan mengubah status pesanan. 
○​ Melihat laporan penjualan.

○​ Mengelola pesanan yang perlu diantarkan. 
○​ Melihat lokasi pengantaran. 
○​ Memperbarui status pengantaran. 
4.​ Dashboard Pengelola Kantin (Super Admin):​
 
○​ Melihat statistik penggunaan aplikasi. 
○​ Mengelola tenant yang terdaftar. 
○​ Mengelola promosi atau program khusus.

-​ Project Manager : 1 orang 
-​ Analys : 1 orang

Server (Hosting dan Database) 
API Gateway 
Sertifikat SSL

Pembuatan materi promosi

disebutkan, diimplementasikan dan siap digunakan oleh seluruh mahasiswa dan tenant di 
kantin kampus.

mengidentifikasi kemungkinan penyebab turunnya kualitas aplikasi tersebut! 

3. Apa peran Quality Audit dalam mencegah masalah seperti ini? Kapan 
sebaiknya audit dilakukan? 
4. Jika Anda adalah project manager, change request seperti apa yang akan 
Anda ajukan untuk memperbaiki situasi ini? Sebutkan minimal 3 poin 
perubahan!

Project Risk Management 
 
Studi Kasus I  
 
Proyek: Implementasi Sistem Informasi Manajemen Rumah 
Sakit (SIMRS) 
 
Latar Belakang Proyek 
Rumah Sakit Umum Daerah (RSUD) Harapan Sehat adalah rumah sakit kelas B milik 
pemerintah daerah dengan kapasitas 350 tempat tidur dan lebih dari 600 tenaga kesehatan. 
Selama ini, seluruh proses administrasi mulai dari pendaftaran pasien, rekam medis, 
pembayaran, hingga pelaporan ke BPJS Kesehatan masih dilakukan secara manual 
menggunakan kertas dan spreadsheet Excel yang tidak terintegrasi. 
Kondisi ini menyebabkan berbagai masalah operasional: antrian pasien yang panjang, rekam 
medis yang sering hilang, kesalahan penagihan, keterlambatan laporan ke BPJS, dan tidak 
adanya data real-time untuk pengambilan keputusan manajemen. 
Deskripsi Proyek 
Nama Proyek  :  Implementasi Sistem Informasi Manajemen Rumah Sakit (SIMRS) 
Terintegrasi 
Sponsor       :  Direktur RSUD Harapan Sehat & Dinas Kesehatan Kabupaten 
Anggaran      :  Rp 2.400.000.000 (Dua Miliar Empat Ratus Juta Rupiah) 
Durasi           :  18 bulan (Januari 2025 — Juni 2026) 
Tujuan proyek adalah mengimplementasikan SIMRS berbasis web yang mengintegrasikan 
seluruh unit layanan rumah sakit, meliputi: 
• 
Modul Pendaftaran & Antrian Pasien (termasuk pendaftaran online) 
• 
Modul Rekam Medis Elektronik (RME) berbasis HL7 FHIR 
• 
Modul Farmasi & Manajemen Obat 
• 
Modul Laboratorium & Radiologi 
• 
Modul Penagihan & Integrasi BPJS Kesehatan 
• 
Modul Laporan Manajemen & Business Intelligence 
• 
Infrastruktur: server on-premise + backup cloud, jaringan LAN seluruh gedung

Tantangan & Konteks Risiko 
Kelompok anda diminta untuk bertindak sebagai konsultan manajemen risiko yang 
ditugaskan oleh Direktur RSUD. Beberapa fakta penting yang perlu dipertimbangkan dalam 
analisis risiko: 
• 
Infrastruktur jaringan RS saat ini sudah berusia 8 tahun dan belum pernah diupgrade 
• 
Sebagian besar staf (±70%) belum pernah menggunakan sistem informasi berbasis 
komputer dalam pekerjaan sehari-hari 
• 
Data rekam medis pasien 10 tahun ke belakang masih dalam format kertas dan perlu 
didigitalisasi 
• 
Kontrak dengan vendor SIMRS belum mencantumkan klausul penalti keterlambatan 
• 
Anggaran proyek bersumber dari APBD yang pencairannya sering terlambat 1-3 
bulan 
• 
RS beroperasi 24/7 sehingga tidak ada downtime untuk migrasi sistem 
• 
Regulasi Kemenkes mengharuskan SIMRS bersertifikasi sebelum go-live 
• 
Tim IT internal RS hanya terdiri dari 3 orang dengan keahlian terbatas di bidang 
sistem enterprise 
 
Berdasarkan studi kasus di atas, buatlah dokumen berikut: 
• 
Risk Management Plan 
mencakup metodologi, peran & tanggung jawab, pendanaan & waktu, kategori risiko, 
probabilitas & dampak, risk appetite stakeholder, dan dokumentasi risiko 
• 
Risk Register 
identifikasi minimal 8 risiko utama proyek dengan detail: nomor, peringkat, nama 
risiko, deskripsi, kategori, akar penyebab, pemicu, respons risiko, pemilik risiko, 
probabilitas, dampak, dan status 
 
Gunakan template yang ada pada slide materi dan sesuaikan dengan konteks proyek 
SIMRS. Pastikan setiap analisis didukung dengan alasan/asumsi yang logis berdasarkan 
fakta dalam studi kasus. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Project Procurement Management 
 
Pilih salah satu (studi kasus IIA atau IIB) 
Studi Kasus II A  
 
Pengembangan Aplikasi Mobile Banking 
Latar Belakang 
PT. Nusantara Digital Bank (NDB) adalah bank umum swasta nasional dengan aset Rp 45 
triliun dan lebih dari 2 juta nasabah aktif yang tersebar di 25 kota besar Indonesia. Saat ini 
NDB hanya melayani transaksi digital melalui internet banking berbasis browser yang sudah 
berusia 6 tahun dan tidak mobile-friendly. Tingkat penurunan (churn) nasabah muda (18-35 
tahun) meningkat 18% dalam dua tahun terakhir, dan survei menunjukkan 74% nasabah 
berpindah ke bank kompetitor karena alasan kemudahan aplikasi mobile. 
Dewan Direksi NDB menyetujui anggaran proyek sebesar Rp 4.800.000.000 untuk 
mengembangkan aplikasi mobile banking baru yang mendukung iOS dan Android. Target 
go-live adalah 12 bulan dari kick-off, dengan fitur utama: transfer dana, pembayaran tagihan, 
top-up e-wallet, informasi rekening/investasi, dan fitur keamanan biometrik. 
Tim IT internal NDB terdiri dari 12 developer (fokus pada backend core banking dan sistem 
legacy), 2 UI/UX designer, dan 1 project manager. Tidak ada satu pun developer internal 
yang berpengalaman dalam pengembangan aplikasi mobile native (Swift/Kotlin). Rekruitmen 
mobile developer senior memerlukan waktu 3-6 bulan dan kompetitif di pasar. 
Keputusan yang Dianalisis 
Pengembangan Aplikasi Mobile Banking NDB untuk platform iOS dan Android, mencakup 
desain UI/UX, pengembangan frontend mobile, integrasi API dengan core banking, 
pengujian keamanan (penetration testing), dan deployment ke App Store & Google Play. 
Opsi yang Dianalisis 
Opsi 1 — MAKE: Merekrut dan membentuk tim mobile developer internal untuk 
mengembangkan aplikasi secara in-house. 
Opsi 2 — BUY: Mengoutsource seluruh pengembangan aplikasi mobile banking kepada 
perusahaan software development spesialis fintech (vendor eksternal). 
Fakta Pendukung Analisis 
• 
Tidak ada developer mobile internal yang berpengalaman saat ini 
• 
Rekruitmen 6 mobile developer senior membutuhkan 3-6 bulan dan biaya kompetitif 
• 
Time-to-market sangat kritis — setiap bulan keterlambatan = potensi kehilangan 
nasabah lebih lanjut 
• 
Regulasi OJK mensyaratkan penetration testing oleh pihak independen bersertifikat 
• 
Maintenance pasca-launch minimal 3 tahun diperlukan 
• 
Vendor fintech terpilih memiliki portofolio 8 aplikasi mobile banking serupa, tim 30 
developer spesialis 
• 
Biaya lisensi tools pengembangan mobile (Xcode, Android Studio, testing framework) 
termasuk dalam estimasi 
 
 
 
 

Studi Kasus II B 
 
Implementasi Sistem ERP untuk Perusahaan Manufaktur 
 
 
Latar Belakang 
PT. Maju Jaya Industri (MJI) adalah perusahaan manufaktur komponen otomotif berskala 
menengah dengan 850 karyawan, 3 pabrik di Jawa dan Sumatera, dan omzet tahunan Rp 
280 miliar. MJI saat ini menggunakan kombinasi software akuntansi standar (Zahir 
Accounting), spreadsheet Excel untuk produksi dan inventori, serta sistem absensi manual. 
Tidak ada integrasi antar sistem, menyebabkan duplikasi data, keterlambatan laporan 
manajemen 3-5 hari, dan sering terjadi kesalahan perencanaan produksi yang 
mengakibatkan overstock atau stockout bahan baku. 
Manajemen MJI memutuskan untuk mengimplementasikan sistem ERP (Enterprise 
Resource Planning) yang terintegrasi mencakup modul: Keuangan & Akuntansi, Manufaktur 
& MRP, Inventori & Gudang, Pembelian, Penjualan, dan SDM & Penggajian. Anggaran yang 
disetujui adalah Rp 3.600.000.000 dengan target implementasi 15 bulan. 
Tim IT MJI terdiri dari 4 orang: 1 IT Manager, 2 sistem analis, dan 1 administrator jaringan. 
Mereka memiliki pengalaman dalam administrasi sistem tetapi tidak ada yang pernah 
mengimplementasikan sistem ERP skala enterprise sebelumnya. MJI mempertimbangkan 
dua pendekatan: membangun sistem ERP custom dari nol menggunakan tim developer 
yang akan direkrut, atau menggunakan ERP berbasis platform open-source (Odoo) yang 
dikonfigurasi dan diimplementasikan oleh partner resmi Odoo. 
Keputusan yang Dianalisis 
Implementasi Sistem ERP Terintegrasi MJI, mencakup seluruh modul bisnis utama 
(Keuangan, Manufaktur, Inventori, Pembelian, Penjualan, SDM), migrasi data dari sistem 
lama, pelatihan pengguna, dan dukungan go-live. 
Opsi yang Dianalisis 
Opsi 1 — MAKE: Bangun sistem ERP custom dari nol dengan merekrut tim developer 
internal (5 developer, 2 sistem analis, 1 database administrator). 
Opsi 2 — BUY: Implementasikan ERP berbasis Odoo Community Edition (open-source) 
melalui partner resmi Odoo Indonesia yang berpengalaman di industri manufaktur. 
Fakta Pendukung Analisis 
• 
Tim IT internal tidak berpengalaman dalam pengembangan maupun implementasi 
ERP enterprise 
• 
Odoo adalah platform ERP open-source terkemuka dengan modul manufaktur 
(MRP) yang sudah terbukti 
• 
Partner Odoo yang diidentifikasi telah mengimplementasikan 15+ proyek manufaktur 
serupa 
• 
Pengembangan ERP custom dari nol biasanya memerlukan 2-4 tahun untuk scope 
yang setara 
• 
Biaya lisensi Odoo Enterprise: Rp 3.500.000/user/tahun untuk 50 user = Rp 
175.000.000/tahun 
• 
Odoo Community (tanpa lisensi) tersedia gratis namun dengan fitur lebih terbatas; 
partner Odoo menyediakan Enterprise 
• 
Migrasi data dari Zahir dan Excel ke ERP baru adalah pekerjaan kompleks yang 
memerlukan keahlian khusus 

• 
Regulasi perpajakan Indonesia (e-Faktur, e-SPT) memerlukan konfigurasi khusus 
yang sudah ada di Odoo Indonesia 
 
 
Gunakan template MAKE-or-BUY decision yang ada pada slide materi dan sesuaikan 
dengan konteks proyek studi kasus IIA/B. Berikan estimasi biaya-biaya yang berlaku saat ini 
dan alasan/asumsi logis berdasarkan fakta dalam studi kasus untuk mendukung analisa 
keputusan MAKE atau BUY.
